title: Call External APIs
summary: Choose an HTTP client, configure it, and send GET and POST requests.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: Master External API Integration in Spring Boot: A Step-by-Step Guide
Engineering Digest: Spring Boot Tutorial: How to Consume External POST APIs Effectively

richText: Call another service
An external API is an API provided by another service. Your application calls it over HTTP.
The provider documentation defines the URL, HTTP method, headers, request body, and response.
Use GET to read a resource. Use POST when the provider requires it for an action or a request body.
A data transfer object (DTO) holds the fields sent or received through the API. Keep provider DTOs separate from database entities.
Put provider calls in a service. Your controller calls that service.
Choose and configure an HTTP client
RestClient sends an HTTP request and waits for the response. It is available from Spring Framework 6.1.
Spring Boot 3.2 includes Spring Framework 6.1. Older course examples use RestTemplate.
WebClient supports nonblocking calls and streaming in reactive applications.
A connect timeout limits how long connection setup can take. A read timeout limits waiting for a response.
Keep API keys in server configuration. Use the authentication header required by the provider.
Use a fixed provider URL. Accepting arbitrary target URLs from users can let them call private services.

example.title: Configure a reusable RestClient
description: Use Spring Boot 3.2+, Spring Framework 6.1+, and Java 17.
Place this bean method in a @Configuration class. Set api.base-url to the provider URL.
explanation: Boot supplies RestClient.Builder. The method creates a client bean for services to inject.
The JDK HTTP client has a three-second connect timeout.
The request factory has a five-second read timeout.

richText: Send GET and POST requests

example.title: Read weather with GET
description: Assume the provider accepts GET /weather?city=Pune and returns {"city":"Pune","temperatureC":26.0}.
The service has an injected RestClient named providerClient.
explanation: queryParam adds the city parameter to the request URL.
body(Weather.class) reads the JSON response into a Weather record.
This call returns the record. It does not print anything.

example.title: Submit text with POST
description: Assume POST /analyses accepts {"text":"Today went well."} and returns {"label":"POSITIVE"}.
The service uses the same injected providerClient.
explanation: contentType declares that the sent body is JSON.
body serializes AnalysisRequest into the request body.
The final body call reads the response into AnalysisResult.

richText: Handle a failed call
RestClient throws for HTTP 4xx and 5xx responses by default.
Check for an empty response body before reading DTO fields.
Use toEntity when you also need the response status or headers.
A timeout does not prove that the provider rejected the request. The provider may already have completed it.
Retry an action only when the provider supports safe duplicate handling, such as an idempotency key. An idempotency key identifies repeated requests as the same operation.
Keep credentials and private request bodies out of logs.
